---
title: "check-quarto-prose.yml"
---

Block a pull request that adds an idiom, cliche or slang phrase to a `.qmd` or
`.md` file, or that puts an example, remark or definition in a notes div.
The house style is plain, literal prose that a reader with English as a second
language, or a literal reading style, can take at face value.
The prose rules themselves live in
[Morrison-Lab/psw](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/psw).
This check enforces two of them mechanically and does not restate them.

## Diff-scoped, like check-typos

Only findings on lines a diff adds are reported, so a first run over an
existing repository does not reflag the prose it already has.
On a pull request the reusable workflow passes `HEAD^1` as `base-ref`:
the base tip GitHub built the merge ref on, which the payload's `base.sha` can lag.
With no `base-ref`, or a `base-ref` this clone cannot see (a shallow clone,
for example), the check is skipped with a warning.
It never falls back to scanning the whole tree.
Pass `base-ref: all` to scan every tracked file once you are ready to clean
the backlog.

A diff-scoped run reads each file as committed at `HEAD`, the same content
the diff was computed from, so an uncommitted edit cannot shift the line
numbers the diff reported.
Only `base-ref: all` reads the working tree.
Lines are counted by newline alone, as git counts them, so a form feed or a
Unicode line separator in a file does not move a finding to the wrong line.

The check is blocking by default.
Only an explicit `fail: false` (trimmed, case-insensitive) turns findings into
warnings.

## Rule 1: notes-div-content

A `::: notes` div, or a `::: {.notes}` div, holds speaker notes.
An example, remark or definition that sits in one is hidden from the rendered
page and cannot be cross-referenced.
The rule reports a notes div when either test is true:

- its body contains a nested div whose id starts with `exm-`, `rem-`, `def-`,
  `thm-` or `exr-`;
- its first non-blank line starts with "Example", "Remark" or "Note:", in any
  case, with optional bold or italic marks (`**Example 1.**`, `__Remark.__`).
  "Examples" and "Remarks" count too.
  "Note that ..." does not, because it has no colon.

The annotation names the line of the nested div or the first line, and gives
the fix: "Use an #exm-, #rem- or #def- div, not a notes div."

The check tracks div nesting by the length of each colon run.
A closing fence ends the nearest open div with the same number of colons, and
any inner div left unclosed ends with it.
A closing fence with no same-length match ends the innermost open div.
So a `:::::` fence that closes an outer notes div ends it even if an inner
`:::` div was never closed, and an `#exm-` div that follows is not read as
inside the notes.
Div fences inside fenced code, HTML comments and display math are ignored.

## Rule 2: banned-idiom

A case-insensitive, whole-phrase match against a list of idioms, cliches and
slang.
The bundled list is
[`banned-idioms.txt`](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/blob/main/check-quarto-prose/banned-idioms.txt).
It holds more than 40 entries, such as `under the hood`, `low-hanging fruit`,
`deep dive`, `at the end of the day`, `rule of thumb` and `a bit of a`.
Read the file for the full set.

List syntax:

- One phrase per line.
  Blank lines and `#` comments are skipped.
- A space or a hyphen in a phrase matches any run of horizontal whitespace
  (spaces, tabs, a non-breaking space), a hyphen, or a single line break, so
  `hand-wavy` also finds `hand wavy` and a phrase wrapped by semantic line
  breaks.
  A phrase never matches across a blank line.
- A word ending in `*` also matches the rest of that word: `cherry-pick*`
  finds `cherry-picked` and `cherry-picking`.
  Use it only where every continuation of the stem is the same idiom.
  The bundled list uses no star: it spells out `dive into`, `dives into`,
  `dived into`, `diving into` and `dove into` instead of `dive*`, because
  the stem would also match "diverges into", and `game changer`,
  `game changers` and `game changing` instead of `game chang*`, which
  would also match "game changes".
- Matching is whole-phrase, so `under the hood` does not match "under the
  hoodie".

The `idioms-file` input replaces the bundled list with your own file in the
same format.
A named file that is missing or lists no phrases is an error, not a silent
fall back to the bundled list.

### What is not scanned

- fenced code blocks, including a fence nested in a longer fence, and
  executable chunks;
- inline code, inline and display math, and HTML comments;
  a `$$` with no closing `$$` hides nothing past the next blank line, the
  next heading or the end of the file, because Pandoc display math cannot
  cross a blank line;
- link destinations and bare URLs, attribute braces such as
  `{#sec-deep-dive}`, shortcodes, and citation or cross-reference keys such as
  `@sec-deep-dive`;
- YAML front matter keys other than `title`, `subtitle` and `description`.

Link text, headings, table cells and image alt text are scanned.

### Exempting a line

Add `<!-- prose-allow: phrase -->` to the line that holds the phrase, for
example when the line quotes someone else.
The comment exempts only the phrases it names (comma-separated), and nothing
else on the line.
A comment alone on its own line exempts the line after it.

For a whole file, use the `allow-file` input: one entry per line, either
`path-glob: phrase` or a bare `phrase` that is allowed everywhere.

## Limits

A phrase list cannot see context.

- Some entries have a literal use.
  A bare "lean" is not listed, because "lean statistics" and "lean on a
library" are literal, so only figurative forms such as `lean toward` are.
  `Rule of thumb` in a quotation, or `red herring` in a discussion of the
fallacy, is a false positive.
  Exempt it.
- A phrase the list does not contain is not flagged, however figurative it is.
  The list is a floor, not a full style check.
- The notes-div test is a first-line and nested-div test.
  An example buried in the middle of plain notes text is not found.
- Matching sees prose line by line after masking.
  A code span that spans two lines is not recognised, so a phrase inside one
may be reported.
- Div attributes such as `title="..."` on a callout are not scanned.

## Inputs

| Input | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `globs` | string | `'*.qmd *.md'` | Space-separated git pathspecs of tracked files to scan (recursive). An empty value uses the default. |
| `paths-ignore` | string | `''` | Comma- or newline-separated globs (`*`, `?`, `**`) of files to skip. |
| `base-ref` | string | `''` | Git ref to diff against; empty uses `HEAD^1`, the base tip of the merge ref, on pull requests and skips on push; `all` scans every tracked file. |
| `idioms-file` | string | `''` | Phrase list replacing the bundled one, relative to the repository root. |
| `allow-file` | string | `''` | `path-glob: phrase` exemptions, relative to the repository root. |
| `fail` | boolean | `true` | Fail the job on a finding (else warn only). |

The composite action takes the same inputs, with `fail` as a string.

## Permissions

Only `contents: read` (the default), so no `permissions:` block is needed.

## Example

```yaml
name: Check Quarto prose
on:
  push: { branches: [main] }
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:
jobs:
  check:
    uses: Morrison-Lab/gha/.github/workflows/check-quarto-prose.yml@v3
    # with:
    #   globs: '*.qmd'
    #   idioms-file: '.github/idioms.txt'
    #   allow-file: '.github/prose-allow.txt'
    #   fail: false
```

See `check-quarto-prose.yml` in
[`examples/`](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/tree/main/examples)
for the full caller stub.
